Architecture Overview

One static Go binary that turns a folder of agent-written HTML into a navigable, searchable, live-reloading site — this page is served by the system it describes.

Context

Coding agents generate architecture docs, ADRs, and PRDs as they work. Those files pile up in a folder and go unread because nothing presents them. Byakugan is the missing presenter: point it at the folder and every subfolder becomes a project, every HTML file a page, everything indexed for instant search. It is built for exactly one use case and refuses to grow into a CMS, wiki, or static-site generator.

Two constraints shape every decision below: zero configuration (byakugan <folder> must always work) and zero dependencies at the edge — no build step, no CDN, no database, one executable you can scp anywhere.

System overview

Five small Go packages sit between two actors: the agent (or engineer) writing HTML into the docs folder, and the browser reading it. The whole runtime is ~1,100 lines of Go plus three embedded UI assets. This page maps the shape; Internals traces the same system at code level, file by file.

The same shape in ASCII — the zero-cost diagram form: no SVG to parse, greppable in the repo, diffable in review, and it renders as fast as text because it is text. Use it for quick topologies; keep the .d-* SVG grammar for figures that earn the polish.

PackageRoleKey decision
mainCLI: flags, subcommands, wiringflags for serving, subcommands for everything else
internal/serverroutes, SSE fan-out, overlay injectionstdlib net/http only
internal/indexscan, extract, snapshotimmutable snapshots swapped atomically
internal/watcherrecursive fs watching300 ms debounce: a burst re-indexes once

The serving pipeline

Four routes cover everything. /api/index.json returns the current snapshot; /events holds an SSE stream open; /__byakugan/* serves the embedded UI; and / is the catch-all page handler shown below.

Injection contract

The overlay snippet is inserted before the last </body> (or appended if none exists). Its CSS variables are scoped to #bk-fab and #bk-drawer — never :root — so the overlay can restyle itself but structurally cannot recolor the document it frames. Theming flows the other way by opt-in: the shared doc.css honors the same data-bk-theme state the toggle writes, so documents flip light/dark with the chrome without the overlay touching them.

Index and search

On start (and on every settled change) the index walks the root, parses each HTML file, and extracts the <title>, the headings, and the first 2,000 characters of visible text. The result is an immutable snapshot swapped in atomically — readers never lock against the scanner.

Search runs in the browser: the full snapshot ships as one JSON payload and search.js ranks matches as you type. For the hundreds-of-pages corpora Byakugan targets, that is faster than any round-trip and keeps the server free of query logic. The landing page and the overlay drawer share the same index and the same ranking.

The whole contract between server and browser is this one payload:

GET /api/index.json
{
  "root": "/team/docs",
  "pageCount": 3,
  "generatedAt": "2026-08-08T14:03:11Z",
  "projects": [{
    "name": "byakugan",
    "updatedAt": "2026-08-08T14:02:58Z",
    "pages": [{
      "path": "byakugan/architecture.html",
      "title": "Architecture Overview",
      "headings": ["Context", "System overview", "…"],
      "text": "first 2,000 chars of visible text…"
    }]
  }]
}

Live reload

An agent regenerating a docs folder writes dozens of files in a burst. The watcher turns that burst into exactly one rebuild and one browser reload.

Two design languages

Everything the user sees follows one settled rule with two voices:

  • Documents are “blueprint editorial” — warm paper, ink serif, drafting-blue accent, semantic diagram colors. The landing page joined this family deliberately: it renders as the dossier’s index sheet (numbered sections, TOC dot leaders, provenance footer) because the index is a document.
  • Chrome is monochrome — the injected overlay (floating button and drawer) frames other people’s pages, so it stays neutral black/white/gray and never competes with the document behind it.

The design system itself ships in the binary as the agent kit: byakugan style prints the shared stylesheet, byakugan rules the authoring guide, and byakugan template prd|adr|architecture|overview a ready-to-paste generation prompt — so any agent can produce pages that belong here, this one included.

Distribution and upgrades

The three UI assets and the agent kit are embedded with go:embed, so a release is a single file per platform, built and published by goreleaser on every tag. At startup the server checks the latest release in the background — silent when offline or current, one log line when newer (--no-update-check opts out). Upgrading is explicit: byakugan upgrade downloads the matching artifact and replaces the running executable in place.

Decision

Stdlib first, one binary, no build step, no external assets. Every feature must survive scp byakugan somewhere && ./byakugan docs on a machine with nothing else installed.

Risk / revisit

The snapshot ships each page’s extracted text (capped at 2,000 chars) to the browser. Beyond a few thousand pages the payload will be felt on page load; the escape hatch is server-side search behind the same /api shape. Not needed at today’s target scale.
